Una nueva especie de Cirsium (Cardueae, Compositae), C. isambertoi de la isla Deserta Grande (Madeira Archipiélago, Portugal) es descrita y fotografiada. # Una nueva especie de Cirsium (Compositae) de Deserta Grande (Archipiélago de Madeira, portugal) ## Autores/as * José Augusto Carvalho Direção Regional do Ordenamento do Território https://orcid.org/0009-0002-8439-7457 * Isamberto Silva Instituto das Florestas e Conservação da Natureza (IFCN, IP-RAM) https://orcid.org/0009-0000-6137-8021 * Alfonso Susanna Botanical Institute of Barcelona (IBB), CSIC-CMCNB https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4717-9063 * Roser Vilatersana Botanical Institute of Barcelona (IBB), CSIC-CMCNB https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5106-8764 ## DOI: https://doi.org/10.3989/collectbot.2025.v44.0013 ## Palabras clave: Archipiélago de Madeira, Asteraceae, Cardueae, Cirsium, Compositae, Islas Desertas, plantas vasculares ## Resumen Una nueva especie de Cirsium (Cardueae, Compositae), C. isambertoi de la isla Deserta Grande (Madeira Archipiélago, Portugal) es descrita y fotografiada. Esta nueva especie es morfológicamente similar a C. latifolium, un endemismo de la Isla de Madeira. La nueva especie difiere de C. latifolium por el tamaño de la planta (30 cm vs. 100 cm) y la forma de las hojas (profundamente pinnatífidas vs. ampliamente dentadas). Debido a la escasa distribución de C. isambertoi y a las amenazas existentes para su hábitat, como la presencia de cabras asilvestradas, la especie se considera en peligro crítico según los criterios y categorías de la UICN. ## Citas Ackerfield, J. Alfonso Susanna * Spanish National Research Council Roser Vilatersana * Institut Botànic de Barcelona Image Download full-text PDFRead full-text ## Abstract and Figures A new species of Cirsium (Cardueae, Compositae), C. isambertoi from Deserta Grande (Madeira Archipelago, Portugal) is described and illustrated. This new species is morphologically similar to C. latifolium, an endemic species from Madeira Island. The new proposed species differs from C. latifolium by the size of the plant (30 cm vs. 100 cm) and the shape of the leaves (deeply pinnatifid vs. broadly dentate). Due to the narrow distribution of C. isambertoi and the existing threats to its habitat such as the presence of feral goats, the species is assessed as Critically Endangered according to IUCN criteria and categories. Etymology: The species is dedicated and named for its rst collector, Isamberto Silva, great connoisseur of the Madeira and the Selvages Archipelagos, and collector of a large number of specimens, both animals (mainly arthropods) and plants, and co-author and collaborator in a large number of articles on this subject. Habitat and ecology: Lava fragment rocks (hill rocks or silt-clay material or pyroclastic rocks) and ba- salt crevices. East slope, facing north, in a valley with high humidity (Fig. 3C). Pollinators observed in-situ: Amegilla maderae (Sichel, 1868), Bombus terrestris (Linnaeus, 1758). Accompanying observed species: Andryala glandulosa Lam. subsp. glandulosa, Lotus argyrodes R. P. Murray, Orobanche minor Sm., Plantago leiopetala Lowe, Sideritis candicans Aiton subsp. crassifolia Lowe, Silene gallica L., Silene uniora Roth, Sonchus ustulatus Lowe, Tolpis fruticosa Schrank, and one liquen, Roccella tinctoria DC. Distribution and preliminary conservation assessment: Cirsium isambertoi is currently known from a single population in the Deserta Grande (Madeira Archipelago, Portugal). During 2013, the number of mature individuals was estimated at 16, of which eight were owering. However, in May and August of 2025, only a single non-owering specimen of C. isambertoi was reported; perhaps the cold weather in the Madeira Archipelago was very intense during this year, which could have affected the population.
